The measured failure mode (from his WSLC/Docker A/B report): letting vLLM auto-allocate at `gpu-memory-utilization=0.80` built a **22.07 GiB KV cache** (536,842-token capacity) and decode collapsed to **25.73 tok/s** while the desktop starved. Pinning the cache explicitly restored ~70 tok/s. So both kits pin, instead of negotiating: | Lever | Value | Effect | |---|---|---| | `GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION` | **0.75** | Leaves ~8 GiB of the card for Windows, the display server and Docker Desktop's WSL VM | | `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` | **4617089843** (exactly 4.30 GiB) | No auto-sizing surprise; reported capacity 102,631 tokens at 100K context (1.03× concurrency). Bumped from 4.25 GiB on 2026-08-22: some Windows hosts need 4.26 GiB for 100K (mamba page alignment + padding layers) and failed boot by ~10 MiB (issue #4) | | `--kv-cache-dtype` | **fp8** | Same requirement as Linux dense 27B — fp16 KV does not fit | | `MAX_NUM_SEQS` | **1** | Single-user desktop serving; this is **not** the concurrent Cn profile | This is the Windows analog of the Linux VRAM gates: on a display-attached GPU, never let the engine size its cache to the card. It is also why the Windows profile runs 100K context rather than the Linux 131,072. ## Quick start Both kits need: Windows 11, a current Intel Arc driver, ≥22 GiB free disk for the ~18.2 GiB model (plus image space), and an ordinary PowerShell window (admin not required). An `HF_TOKEN` read token is optional — the model is public; it only improves download rate limits. The complete authored steps are below; each kit's `README.md` / `README.html` is the canonical copy. **Docker Desktop (recommended):** install Docker Desktop from , select the Linux/WSL 2 engine, start it, then: ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Setup-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 # builds image, probes B70, downloads model, starts server .\Test-CookbookDecode.ps1 # optional: exact-token decode benchmark (cookbook method) .\Stop-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 # stops server, keeps container + compiled-graph cache ``` **WSLC (experimental):** ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Setup-Qwen38-WSLC.ps1 .\Stop-Qwen38.ps1 -ReleaseGpuMemory # terminating the WSLC session is what returns VRAM to Windows ``` Endpoint (both): `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`, served model name `qwen38`. Tool calling is on (`qwen3_coder` parser), vision is off, thinking is on with a low default reasoning effort (template below). ## Upgrade from 2026.08.18 — draft INT4 + prefix cache The 18 August kit already works. This is the next image, not a new install. What changed in **2026.08.19**: | Piece | 2026.08.18 (what you have) | 2026.08.19 (rebuild this) | |---|---|---| | Patches | MTP nightly + MTP boundary | those two, plus mixed-split v5, plus draft-INT4 S+M1 | | Draft head | BF16 (`B70_MTP_BF16_DRAFT=1`) | still that checkpoint; the **draft** is requantized to INT4 at start (`DRAFT_INT4=1`) | | Prefix cache | off | **on** (real multi-turn sessions). Turn it off only for a cold decode test | | Sampling | template only | `--generation-config auto` (Qwen thinking / non-thinking defaults) | | Image tag | `qwen38-b70-docker:2026.08.18` / `qwen38-b70-friendly:2026.08.18` | `…:2026.08.19` | | Display-safe VRAM | 0.75 + 4.25 GiB fp8 KV, 100K, MTP4, C1 | same pin; KV default later bumped 4.25 → 4.30 GiB for headroom (see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting-windows)) | Linux, same overlay, C1, n=5, cache **off**: **112.65** vs matched BF16-draft **81.20** tok/s at p512/g128. Prefill is flat. Quality KEEP on the 12/15 coding gate. That is a Linux campaign, not a Windows re-measure. On Windows expect “noticeably faster than your ~70”, not a copied 112. Prefix cache is for **follow-up turns**, not a first-token speed-up. Leave it on for Pi / Open WebUI / anything with a system prompt. For `Test-CookbookDecode.ps1` (cold unique prompts) set `-PrefixCache 0` so the cell matches the Linux speed card. **Do not** `docker start` the old container after a rebuild. Docker keeps the 18 August entrypoint until you recreate. ### Docker Desktop (recommended) In the kit folder (`windows/Qwen38-Docker-Standalone/` if you cloned, or the unzipped kit after `git pull`): ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Upgrade-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 ``` That rebuilds `qwen38-b70-docker:2026.08.19`, **removes** `qwen38-b70-docker-test`, and starts a new container with `DRAFT_INT4=1` and prefix cache **on**. Model files on disk are reused. Manual equivalent: ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Build-Qwen38Image-Docker.ps1 .\Start-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 -Recreate # optional: cold decode test (prefix cache off) .\Start-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 -Recreate -PrefixCache 0 .\Test-CookbookDecode.ps1 ``` Confirm the overlay actually ran: ```powershell docker logs qwen38-b70-docker-test | findstr /C:"draft-INT4" ``` You want: `[start] draft-INT4 S+M1 overlay ENABLED`. Fall back to the 18 August draft (BF16, still the same model files): ```powershell .\Start-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 -Recreate -DraftInt4 0 ``` ### WSLC (experimental) ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Upgrade-Qwen38-WSLC.ps1 ``` WSLC already deletes the previous container on start. Confirm with `wslc logs qwen38-b70-friendly`. WSLC was ~26 tok/s on 18 August; this overlay does not fix that runtime. ### Fresh install (never ran the 18 August kit) Same as before: `.\Setup-Qwen38-Docker.ps1`. Setup now builds **2026.08.19** with the overlay and prefix cache on. You still install Docker Desktop first. --- ## Full step-by-step (as Ian authored and tested it) Transcribed from the kit READMEs so this page is self-contained. Work in the kit folder you downloaded (or `windows/Qwen38-*-Standalone/` from this repo). ### Step 0 — shared preparation (both paths) 1. **Open PowerShell in the extracted kit folder** (an ordinary window; administrator mode is not normally required). 2. **Optional: a Hugging Face read token** (higher rate limits; the model itself is public): 1. Sign in at , open , **Create new token** → type **Read**. It begins with `hf_`. 2. Set it for this window only: `$env:HF_TOKEN = "hf_your_read_token_here"` — or permanently: `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("HF_TOKEN", "hf_your_read_token_here", "User")` (permanent changes are visible to **new** processes — reopen PowerShell). 3. Verify without printing it: `if ($env:HF_TOKEN) { "HF_TOKEN is set" } else { "HF_TOKEN is not set" }` 4. Treat it like a password; revoke and replace it if it is ever exposed. 3. **Optional: place the model manually** instead of downloading — copy the repository contents into the kit's `.\models\Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4\` folder. It must contain `config.json`, all five `model-0000x-of-00005.safetensors` shards, the shard index and tokenizer files. ### Path A — Docker Desktop (recommended) 1. **Install Docker Desktop manually** from only. Choose the **Linux/WSL 2** engine, start Docker Desktop and wait until it reports the engine is running. 2. **Check access** in a new ordinary PowerShell window: ```powershell docker context use desktop-linux docker info ``` If `docker info` reports permission denied, an administrator can add your Windows user to Docker's access group: ```powershell net localgroup docker-users "$env:USERNAME" /add ``` Then **sign out and back in (or reboot)**, start Docker Desktop, and run `docker info` again. 3. **Run the installer** (start Docker Desktop first): ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Setup-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 ``` It verifies Docker, builds the pinned image, mounts the minimum WSL GPU interfaces (`/dev/dxg`, `/usr/lib/wsl/lib`, `/usr/lib/wsl/drivers`, read-only; **no `--privileged`**), runs a real XPU calculation, downloads the model if necessary, and starts the server. Partial downloads are retained for resumption. 4. **Use it.** Endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`, model name `qwen38`, automatic tool choice with the `qwen3_coder` parser, vision disabled. 5. **Daily controls:** ```powershell .\Start-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 # starts or restarts; preserves the compiled-graph cache .\Stop-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 # stops; keeps the stopped container for fast restart .\Build-Qwen38Image-Docker.ps1 # rebuild the pinned image only .\Test-CookbookDecode.ps1 # exact-token decode benchmark ``` The first image build and model download take a long time; model loading is several minutes because the 18.2 GiB checkpoint is read from the Windows bind mount. Keep the stopped container rather than removing it to preserve the compiled graph cache. ### Path B — Microsoft WSLC (experimental) 1. **Prerequisites:** Windows 11 with Microsoft WSLC installed and working, Arc Pro B70 with a current Windows driver. 2. **Run the installer:** ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass .\Setup-Qwen38-WSLC.ps1 ``` It builds the pinned image, verifies a real XPU allocation/compute probe (including the B70 PCI ID `0xe223` when the driver hides the marketing name), downloads the model when absent, and starts the server with the friendly profile. 3. **Daily controls:** ```powershell .\Start-Qwen38.ps1 -MtpTokens 4 -MaxModelLength 100000 -GpuMemoryUtilization 0.75 -KvCacheMemoryGiB 4.3 -KvCacheDtype fp8 .\Stop-Qwen38.ps1 .\Stop-Qwen38.ps1 -ReleaseGpuMemory # terminates the WSLC session to return ALL GPU memory to Windows .\Test-B70Gpu.ps1 # standalone B70 passthrough + XPU probe .\Test-CookbookDecode.ps1 ``` Startup and model download can take several minutes; the setup script prints progress and warns immediately if `HF_TOKEN` is unavailable. ## What the kits pin (provenance) | Component | Exact value | |---|---| | Base image | `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu@sha256:f01e24f6c7ff01f1e0662234255a1372297d1dbd89d003cf13c8fad3eab1ba4f` — the **same digest as the Linux Qwen3.8 champion row** in [IMAGE-AND-PATCH-MATRIX.md](../IMAGE-AND-PATCH-MATRIX.md) | | vLLM / kernels in image | `0.27.2rc1.dev77+gac7509e2b` / `0.1.12.3` (verified in-image, not from the tag) | | Patches | MTP nightly + boundary (commit `5c6b6b1`), then mixed-split v5 (`db20e00`), then draft-INT4 S+M1 (`aa363ca`). SHA-256-verified at build after LF normalization. WSLC downloads the five files hash-pinned; Docker verifies the bundled copies | | Model | [`SergiioB/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4-sym-G128-MTP-BF16`](https://huggingface.co/SergiioB/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4-sym-G128-MTP-BF16) @ revision `9d189a60e4c0ad7f9f47cd94bfa393ca10b3924e` (5 shards) — **same files as 2026.08.18** | | Draft profile | **Draft-INT4 S+M1 on** (`DRAFT_INT4=1`). The checkpoint still ships a BF16 MTP head; the overlay requantizes only the draft at start. Set `DRAFT_INT4=0` to recover the 18 August BF16-draft path | | Prefix cache | **On** for serving (`PREFIX_CACHE=1`). Set `PREFIX_CACHE=0` only for a cold unique-prompt decode test | | Author's test machine | Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, WSL 2.9.4.0, Intel driver 32.0.101.8805 (2026-07-07), Docker client 29.7.2 | Served flags (via `container/start.sh` in both kits): MTP4 (`num_speculative_tokens 4`), `--quantization gptq --dtype float16`, `--max-model-len 100000`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, `--enable-prefix-caching` (default; `--no-enable-prefix-caching` if `PREFIX_CACHE=0`), `--generation-config auto`, `--language-model-only`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, XPU graphs on, expandable segments on. ## Line endings (Git for Windows) The cookbook stores every text file as **LF**. Git for Windows defaults to `core.autocrlf=true`, so a clone can rewrite working-tree files to CRLF. That used to fail SHA-256 checks on the five pinned patches and to break `container/start.sh` inside the Linux image (`/usr/bin/env bash^M`). The repo now pins LF via `.gitattributes`. The build scripts also rewrite patches, Dockerfiles, and container scripts to LF before hashing or `COPY`, and both Dockerfiles strip CR as a last line of defense. If you cloned before this fix, `git pull` and rebuild (`.\Upgrade-Qwen38-Docker.ps1` or `.\Upgrade-Qwen38-WSLC.ps1`). Do not re-download the model. ## Windows-specific engineering inside the kits - **WSLC exposes XPU compute but not Linux `/dev/dri` DRM nodes.** The kits force oneCCL away from drmfd IPC (`CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=sockets` and friends) and ship `patch_xpu_single_gpu_warmup.py`, which skips vLLM's one-rank oneCCL warm-up `all_reduce` on `world_size == 1` (a no-op reduction whose IPC path would otherwise fail). - **Docker needs only the minimum GPU surface:** `/dev/dxg` plus read-only `/usr/lib/wsl/lib` and `/usr/lib/wsl/drivers`. No `--privileged`. - **An NVIDIA GPU in the same Windows machine does not take over.** WSL shares `libnvidia-ml.so.1` with the container, so vLLM's CUDA probe sees the NVIDIA card and stops with `Only one platform plugin can be activated, but got: ['cuda', 'xpu']`. `patch_xpu_only_platform.py` returns no CUDA platform when `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=xpu`, which both start scripts set (issue #15). - **B70 identity check tolerates Windows drivers:** `diagnose.py` accepts the marketing name **or** the Battlemage PCI ID `0xe223` (some Windows drivers expose only the device ID), then runs a real XPU allocation/compute probe before any model load. - **Low-reasoning default without touching the model:** a build-time copy of the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja` with the single anchor `reasoning_effort|default('xhigh')` → `'low'` (the kit refuses to patch if the anchor count is not exactly 1 — verified against the pinned revision). - **Slow first model load is expected:** weights are read from a Windows bind mount through WSL's 9P file system; the Docker kit preserves the stopped container to keep its compiled-graph cache. ## Troubleshooting (Windows) **Red `NativeCommandError` text while the container is actually fine.** vLLM (and `docker`/`wslc` themselves) write progress and INFO lines to stderr, and PowerShell with `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` can promote that harmless stderr text into a terminating `NativeCommandError`, killing the readiness loop of older kit copies. The start and download scripts now capture native stderr inside a `Continue` scope, so `git pull` fixes it. If you see the red text on an old copy while `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models` responds, the server is fine — update the kit and rerun. **Intel NEO `linear_stream.h` abort under sustained load.** With XPU graphs on and Level Zero's default immediate command lists, long agent sessions could abort the engine (`Abort was called at 90 line in file: .../linear_stream.h`, then `EngineDeadError`). Both start scripts now set `SYCL_PI_LEVEL_ZERO_USE_IMMEDIATE_COMMANDLISTS=0` by default — the reporter-verified workaround from issue #6, which stopped the aborts while keeping graph-enabled speed (~104–106 tok/s short decode). Existing containers keep their old env: recreate with `.\Start-Qwen38-Docker.ps1 -Recreate` (or the WSLC twin) to pick it up. **Throughput and MTP acceptance degrade over hours, server stays alive (Issue #6).** In controlled continuous testing without agent harnesses (repeated fixed-shape benchmark runs over hours): - **INT4 draft (`-DraftInt4 1`):** Experienced a gradual throughput drop followed by a severe speculative token acceptance collapse (falling from ~99% to ~59% by Cycle 5, reducing decode to ~60 tok/s). - **BF16 draft (`-DraftInt4 0`):** Maintained **100% MTP acceptance** throughout 18 cycles, though underlying runtime state accumulation showed a gradual ~19.9% throughput drift (77.3 -> 61.9 tok/s). - **Restoration:** A quick container restart (`.\Stop-Qwen38-Docker.ps1` followed by `.\Start-Qwen38-Docker.ps1`) immediately clears accumulated Level Zero / allocator state and completely restores 100% throughput and normal MTP acceptance. **Recommendation for long-running / agentic workloads:** 1. Use `-DraftInt4 0` (BF16 draft) for multi-hour stability. Keep `-DraftInt4 1` for short-session / benchmark speed. 2. The default **100,000 context** with explicit **4.30 GiB FP8 KV cache** and `GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.75` is the proven sweet spot on single-card B70 Windows setups, leaving ~8 GiB for the OS and display. 3. If running continuous 24/7 daemon tasks, schedule a periodic container restart. ## Measured results — self-reported, one Windows machine > **Evidence class: external self-report.** These numbers are Ian's, measured > on his Windows 11 machine with `Test-CookbookDecode.ps1` (exact-token > prompts, streaming client timing, same method as the cookbook). They are not > a B70-DOCS campaign and have not been independently reproduced. C1, cache > off, MTP4, 100K, fp8 KV, 4.25 GiB explicit cache. | Scenario | WSLC | Docker Desktop | Docker advantage | |---|---:|---:|---:| | p512/g128 decode, after 60 s idle | 25.76 tok/s | 69.76 tok/s | 2.71× | | p512/g128 decode, best initial | 48.18 tok/s | 71.84 tok/s (median of 5) | 1.49× | | p8192/g128 decode | 26.91 tok/s | 64.26 tok/s (median of 3) | 2.39× | | p8192 time to first token | 348.82 s | 4.42–4.51 s | ~78× | Docker Desktop consistency on the recommended config: short-prompt median 71.84 (range 71.63–72.94, TTFT 0.356–0.359 s); after idle 69.76 (69.53–71.01); sustained g1024 68.45 / 67.08; p8192 64.42 / 64.26 / 64.08. MTP acceptance read 100% throughout (greedy, repetitive filler prompts — the acceptance maximum; real prompts sample lower on every measured stack). **Directional only:** the Linux champion in the **BF16-draft** profile class measured **83.7** tok/s C1 p512/g128 (n=5). Windows Docker at ~70 is ~15% below that cell — different OS, driver, scheduler and file path, plus a single-machine self-report versus a controlled campaign. Do not compute a precise "Windows tax" from these two cells. The Linux **draft-INT4 S+M1** overlay is a later matched n=5: **112.65** vs **81.20** at the same p512/g128 cell (cache off). Windows 2026.08.19 ships that overlay; it has **not** been re-measured on Ian's machine. Do not put 112.65 in a Windows table until `Test-CookbookDecode.ps1` is re-run on 2026.08.19. The WSLC slowness is documented for Microsoft in [`windows/Qwen38-WSLC-Standalone/WSLC-Performance-Bug-Report.md`](../../windows/Qwen38-WSLC-Standalone/WSLC-Performance-Bug-Report.md) (same image, model, driver and benchmark on both runtimes; suspects GPU memory placement / scheduling inside the WSLC runtime). Until Microsoft responds, **Docker Desktop is the Windows path**. ## Vendored copies — fixes applied The originals are Ian's zips (`Qwen38-WSLC-Standalone-2026.08.18.zip`, `Qwen38-Docker-Standalone-2026.08.18.zip`). The vendored trees started byte-equal to them except: 1. **`Qwen38-Docker-Standalone/Test-CookbookDecode.ps1`** — added `Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Net.Http`. The WSLC twin already had it; without it Windows PowerShell 5.1 can fail to resolve `[Net.Http.HttpClient]` used by the streaming benchmark. 2. **`Qwen38-WSLC-Standalone/Start-Qwen38.ps1`** — `--publish` changed from `${Port}:8000` (all interfaces) to `127.0.0.1:${Port}:8000`, matching the Docker kit and the documented endpoint. The API has no authentication and must not be LAN-visible by default. *(Standard docker publish syntax, but not re-tested on `wslc.exe` — re-run once before redistributing the zip.)* 3. Provenance header added to both kit `README.md` files (this page). **2026.08.19 overlay** (this page's upgrade): both kits now also ship `patch_gdn_mixed_split_v5.py`, `patch_draft_lmhead_int4.py`, `patch_draft_mtp_int4.py`; `container/start.sh` applies them and defaults `DRAFT_INT4=1` / `PREFIX_CACHE=1`; image tag `2026.08.19`; `Upgrade-Qwen38-*.ps1` rebuilds and recreates so a leftover 18 August container cannot silently keep the old entrypoint. The Microsoft bug report is unchanged evidence. ## Files ```text windows/ Qwen38-WSLC-Standalone/ WSLC kit: Setup/Build/Download/Start/Stop, Test-B70Gpu, Smoke-Test, Test-CookbookDecode, bug report Qwen38-Docker-Standalone/ Docker Desktop kit: Setup/Build/Download/Start/Stop, Smoke-Test, Test-CookbookDecode (both) container/ start.sh, diagnose.py, oneCCL warm-up skip, XPU-only platform guard, low-reasoning template patch (both) patches/ five hash-pinned files: MTP nightly, MTP boundary, mixed-split v5, draft lmhead INT4, draft MTP INT4 (both) Upgrade-Qwen38-*.ps1 rebuild image 2026.08.19 and recreate the container (both) models/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4/ PLACE_MODEL_FILES_HERE.txt (model not bundled) ``` ## Credits Windows packages devised and tested by **Ian Hudson — [aitesthive.com](https://aitesthive.com)**, 2026-08-18. Cookbook section, vendoring and fixes by the B70 cookbook maintainers, 2026-08-19. Windows and the Windows logo are trademarks of the Microsoft group of companies. The logo is used here nominatively to identify compatibility with Microsoft Windows; this independent project is not endorsed by Microsoft.

docs.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — AP-Q4_K_XL dual-card placement (capability, no performance claim)
docs.text:
# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next — AP-Q4_K_XL dual-card placement (capability, no performance claim)

Status: **capability — load + coherence verified; no performance claim on this placement.**

The AP-Q4_K_XL GGUF is ~94 GB — larger than one 32 GB card. This recipe places it across
two Arc Pro B70s with a bounded CPU offload and is the only known-working load for this
artifact on this hardware class.

## Requirements

- Binary: a `qwen4exp`-capable llama.cpp SYCL build, icx/icpx 2026.1.1
  (sha256 `7c2d6adc4ac5dfa6f1deb8db8d545d8e4cae390ed9c1cd255d1e7f71a83e84a1`).
- Model: `Signal-3.8-Flash-Next-AP-Q4_K_XL.gguf`
  (101,142,769,984 bytes, sha256 `427a7a10dd5a98d77c71be62a89d14e7408fc61a84c6efe889393852282cd3c6`).

## The placement that works (and the one that does not)

A plain 49/51 layer split **overfills both cards** (per-card weight use ≈34.6 / 32.3 GiB
before KV) and dies at padded-tensor allocation. The corrected placement offloads the
PLE and the expert weights of the first and last six blocks to CPU:

```bash
llama-server -m Signal-3.8-Flash-Next-AP-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --device SYCL0,SYCL1 --tensor-split 49,51 --split-mode layer -ngl 99 \
  -ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU,blk\.([0-5]|4[2-7])\.ffn_(up|gate|down)_exps\.weight=CPU' \
  -c 8192 -fa on -t 6 -tb 14 -np 1 -b 512 -ub 512 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q4_1 \
  --no-warmup --metrics --slots --jinja \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8010
```

Observed load state: /health in ~75–90 s, >3.3 GiB free on the fuller card, no
DEVICE_LOST/OOM lines. For an 8K-prompt cell use `-c 9216`.

## Verification gates this recipe passed

1. Fixed three-prompt coherence trio at temperature 0 (answers: `B70-FLASH-OK`,
   `703`, `Paris` — this model emits a short reasoning block first; give it
   `max_tokens ≥ 256` or visible content can come back empty).
2. Offline exact-token calibration (512 and 8192) with a live `/tokenize`
   id-sequality gate before any measured request.

## Scope and limits

- This is a **capacity** recipe (94 GB across two 32 GB cards). It makes no speed
  claim; treat any per-stream numbers you measure on this placement as
  placement-specific, not as the model's or the hardware's ceiling.
- The MTP GGUF exists for this model but is not part of this placement record.
- Failure signature of the wrong placement (early-block-only offload): instant
  `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` in `ggml_backend_sycl_buffer_init_tensor` memset,
  from padded-tensor allocation overfill.

docs.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on two Arc Pro B70s
docs.text:
# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on two Arc Pro B70s

llama.cpp SYCL, one request at a time (`-np 1`). 8K / 16K / 128K on this page
are **context windows**, not concurrency. The same patched tree serves all
three. The n=5 leader cells happen to be 8K decode and 16K prefill — that is
not a 16K cap.

This is a different model from [Qwen3.8-27B](../qwen38-27b/README.md). The
numbers are llama.cpp engine timings, not vLLM client rates.

> **2026-09-11 update — MTP + fused multi-token MoE kernel.** The recipe below
> (no-spec, pinned build `9723942`) still works and is the fallback. The new
> leader route is upstream main `52d4268` + a qwen4exp MTP port + a local fused
> multi-token `MUL_MAT_ID` kernel: **33.25 tok/s** decode (P512/G128 C1, code
> task, n=5 median; prose 30.68) vs **23.38** on the old build (+42%), **585.9
> tok/s** prefill (F16 path), and the **first completed near-boundary 128K**
> (P~120.7K, 18.38 tok/s, n=5). See "MTP + kernel update" section. The main
> GGUF still carries no MTP tensors — the draft is a separate head GGUF.

![Leaders](../assets/b70-qwen38-flash-next-dashboard.svg)

![Prefill and decode vs context](../assets/b70-qwen38-flash-next-context.svg)

## MTP + kernel update (2026-09-11)

![MTP progression](../assets/b70-qwen38-flash-next-mtp-progression.svg)

Same serving contract as below (C1, n=5 fresh-server medians unless noted,
t=1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20, ignore_eos, exact token counts, zero cache
reuse, 195 W, PLE pre-warmed). Matched natural-prompt cells (prose/code
tasks), not filler.

| Build | Cell | Decode | vs old build 23.38 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| pinned `9723942` (recipe below) | 8K p512/g128 | 23.38 | base |
| upstream `52d4268`, no-spec | 8K p512/g128 | 26.86 (n=3) | +15% |
| `52d4268` + MTP tuned, warm | 8K p512/g128 | 29.90 (n=3) | +28% |
| + **wired multi-token kernel**, warm | 8K p512/g128 | **37.37** (n=3, peak 43.76) | **+60%** |
| + wired kernel, matched **prose** | 8K p512/g128 | **30.68** (n=5) | +31% |
| + wired kernel, matched **code** | 8K p512/g128 | **33.25** (n=5) | **+42%** |

![Decode vs context](../assets/b70-qwen38-flash-next-mtp-context.svg)

| Context / input | Pre-wiring | Wired | Gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c8, P~0.5K code | 23.38 (old build) | 33.25 | +42% |
| c16, P~8.5K prose | 21.38 | **30.85** (n=5) | +44% |
| c131072, P~120.7K near-boundary | 18.53 (old build) | **18.38** (n=5, first completed 120K) | ~0% (attention/serial-bound) |

Prefill unchanged-best on the F16 binary: **585.9 tok/s** cold input
(P9096/G128/C1, n=3; old build was 594.49 n=5 — same class).

![Kernel A/B](../assets/b70-qwen38-flash-next-mtp-kernel-ab.svg)

**Why it is faster:** upstream MTP verify runs every routed MoE op as
`ids=[10,1]` even for multi-row verify batches — the 3D `src1 [n_embd,1,T]`
form hid behind the `ne12 == 1` gate and fell to the counting-sort path
(D2H expert ids + host sort + grouped GEMM, ~144 ops/round). The local patch
fuses those into one multi-token GEMV: verify-round cost **118 → ~85 ms**,
measured by per-request acceptance/counters; env kill-switch
`GGML_SYCL_MT_OFF=1` reproduces the pre-wiring numbers. Quality battery:
42/42 code tests, output divergence inside the spec-OFF envelope.

![Prefill F16](../assets/b70-qwen38-flash-next-mtp-prefill-f16.svg)

### MTP recipe delta (on top of the flags below)

- Tree: upstream main `52d42686560a9e8f441f9b9780c8890c37d2802d` (the pinned
  `9723942` patches are superseded — the fused IQ3_S/IQ4_NL MMVQ is upstream).
- Patches, in this order, from the cookbook checkout:

```bash
git checkout 52d42686560a9e8f441f9b9780c8890c37d2802d
git apply patches/llamacpp-sycl/qwen4exp-mtp-draft-head.patch
git apply patches/llamacpp-sycl/sycl-fused-mmvq-mt.patch
```

  Copy the two files next to the llama.cpp tree, or pass the cookbook path
  to `git apply`. Do not apply `flashnext-arch-overlay.patch` or
  `sycl-fused-mmvq-and-gpu-group.patch` on this pin.

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `qwen4exp-mtp-draft-head.patch` | `86fccb037a98605079b2b0178cc21d910341f9a0b060e5b534da499a0a2c1222` |
| `sycl-fused-mmvq-mt.patch` | `126632bbf5ec5fe16401254d262dacba1a4b6728756400ba65010faa1c30516e` |

  First file: qwen4exp MTP draft-head (adapted from
  [dzannotti's patch](https://huggingface.co/dzannotti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTP-GGUF):
  MTP-only tensor walk, `graph_mtp`, `DECODER_MTP` routing, `t_h_nextn`
  handover, two drift fixes for post-b10612 upstream).
  Second file: fused multi-token MoE kernel (`mul_mat_vec_q_moe_mt` +
  `ggml_sycl_mul_mat_vec_q_id_mt`, M=2..8, gate-up + grouped down forms).
  Wrapper accepts 3D `src1 [n_embd,1,T]` and `[n_embd,k,T]`.
  `GGML_SYCL_MT_OFF=1` falls back to the counting-sort path (MTP accept
  stays high, tok/s drops below no-spec). Full inventory:
  [`results/qwen38-flash-next-mtp-kernel-v1/summary.json`](../../results/qwen38-flash-next-mtp-kernel-v1/summary.json).
- Draft head:
  [`dzannotti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTP-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/dzannotti/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MTP-GGUF)
  `Q4_K_M` (2.44 GiB, SHA-256 `1f2a6991…f4c02`), served with
  `-md <draft.gguf> -ngld 999 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3
  --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 --spec-draft-backend-sampling --spec-draft-device SYCL1`.
- **`LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1` is mandatory** with quantized KV on qwen4exp
  (load/decode crash otherwise, upstream issue #21038).
- Sampling defaults follow the HF card's **thinking** mode (reasoning on):
  `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0` — these are baked into the
  desktop launcher and match every measured cell on this page.
- Decode binary: FP32 (`GGML_SYCL_F16=OFF`). Prefill binary: F16, no spec.
- 128K with MTP needs `-b/-ub 1024` and fits only as a capacity observation
  (GPU1 transient free 391 MiB at demand time; all 5 samples valid).

Catalog records:
[`qwen38-flash-next-mtp-kernel-decode-v1`](../BENCHMARK-CATALOG.md),
`-prefill-v1`, `-c128-nearboundary-v1`. LocalMaxxing: matched decode record
`cmtwyygmq0ah0ps01vvutjf7u` (APPROVED).

## What we measured

Self-reported, n=5 after one discarded warmup. Sampling: temperature 1.0,
`top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `ignore_eos`, exactly 128 output tokens, cache off.

| Build | Context | Prompt / output | Decode | Cold input |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| FP32 (`GGML_SYCL_F16=OFF`) | 8K | p512 / g128 | **23.38** tok/s (23.22–23.73) | 183.98 |
| F16 (`GGML_SYCL_F16=ON`) | 16K | actual p9096 / g128 | 20.34 tok/s | **594.49** (594.11–595.45) |

`GGML_SYCL_F16` is a compile-time SYCL flag, not the weight dtype. Build one binary per server. F16 wins prefill; FP32 is a bit faster on decode. The F16 16K server is also the 20.3 tok/s decode / 594 tok/s prefill pair.

Average card draw on those cells was about 97–99 W (GPU 0) and 108 W (GPU 1)
against a 195 W cap. With the 88 GiB model resident, GPU 1 package sat near
62 °C at idle.

Smoke on every measured server: `B70-FLASH-OK`, `37*19=703`, `Paris`.

Raw JSON: [results/qwen38-flash-next-dual-b70-c1/](../../results/qwen38-flash-next-dual-b70-c1/).

## Prerequisites

| Need | What we used |
|---|---|
| GPUs | **Two** Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB (64 GB combined). Layer split, no GPU P2P. One card cannot hold this GGUF. |
| VRAM | ~32,656 MiB visible per card. Empty-card `visible_avail` ~31 GiB on **both** cards before load. |
| Host RAM | **32 GB is enough** with mmap. Do **not** `--mlock` or `--no-mmap` — the file is 88 GiB. The ~36 GiB N-gram table (shard `00002`, Q5_1) is mmap-backed and served from host memory/disk, never VRAM. |
| Disk | **≥110 GiB free**: 88.03 GiB GGUF (33 shards) + ~20 GiB for llama.cpp source and **two** SYCL builds. KV cache lives entirely in VRAM, not on disk. Shard `00002` (N-gram table) alone is ~38.4 GiB. |
| CPU | 16-thread class (Ryzen 7 5700X3D here). Server uses `-t 6 -tb 14`. |
| OS / driver | Linux, `xe` driver, Level Zero. `sycl-ls` must list both B70s as SYCL0 / SYCL1. |
| Compiler | Intel oneAPI **IntelLLVM 2026.0.0**, CMake, git, `huggingface-cli`. |

This is not the Qwen3.8-27B vLLM recipe.

**F16 vs FP32** is not the GGUF. Weights stay mixed IQ3_S / IQ4_NL. `GGML_SYCL_F16` is a compile-time SYCL math flag, so you build two binaries. F16 wins prefill; FP32 is a bit faster on decode.

## Hardware and weights

- Two Intel Arc Pro B70 32 GB, CPU-attached x8 + x8, no GPU P2P.
- GGUF: [`AtomicChat/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF)
  folder `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64`, revision
  `142262902a46f7daed19c79d0771534c8106ad59` (33 shards, 88.03 GiB).
- Mixed quant: gate/up **IQ3_S**, down **IQ4_NL**. The folder name `Q4_K_M` is
  not a uniform Q4_K_M file.
- KV: `q8_0` K + `q4_1` V. Flash attention on. The main GGUF carries no MTP
  tensors; the MTP route uses the separate dzannotti draft head (see the
  2026-09-11 update above).

#### N-gram (per-layer token embedding) table

The N-gram lookup table lives **on disk, not in VRAM**. It is a single tensor
`per_layer_token_embd.weight`, dims `[160, 320001536]` (160 per-layer rows × a
320 M vocab-lookup axis, ~51.2 B elements), quantized **Q5_1** (GGUF dtype 7),
and it occupies shard **`00002`** of 33 entirely on its own (~38.4 GiB on disk;
BF16 source would be ~95.4 GiB). Everything after it (`00003`+) holds the layer
weights: routed/shared experts IQ3_S (gate/up) + IQ4_NL (down), and Q8_0
attention/SSM/head projections. Shard `00001` holds only the LM head.

It never enters GPU memory. The serve line forces it to host RAM with
`-ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU'`; at ~35.8 GiB Q5_1 it cannot fit in the
combined ~65 GiB VRAM next to the experts and the `q8_0`/`q4_1` KV cache, so
llama.cpp memory-maps it from the GGUF and serves the lookups from CPU/disk.
Treat it as a separate placement and quantization axis from the GPU-resident
weights (see `docs/qwen38-27b/README.md` for the sibling 27B route; do not mix).

## Reproduce

### 1. Weights

```bash
huggingface-cli download AtomicChat/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF \
  --revision 142262902a46f7daed19c79d0771534c8106ad59 \
  --include 'Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64/*' \
  --local-dir "$HOME/models/qwen38-flash-next-m64"
```

llama.cpp split GGUF: pass **only the first shard** to `-m`. The other 32 files
must stay in the same directory with the same prefix. The first file’s metadata
points at `00002`…`00033`; llama.cpp opens them from that folder.

```bash
export MODEL="$HOME/models/qwen38-flash-next-m64/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64-00001-of-00033.gguf"
ls "$(dirname "$MODEL")" | wc -l   # expect 33
```

### 2. llama.cpp pin

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
cd llama.cpp
git checkout 9723942adc518b43c4b95dc4dce6906903eb5e09
```

### 3. Patches (this cookbook, in this order)

```bash
git apply patches/llamacpp-sycl/flashnext-arch-overlay.patch
git apply patches/llamacpp-sycl/sycl-fused-mmvq-and-gpu-group.patch
# run from the cookbook checkout; both files are in-repo under patches/llamacpp-sycl/
```

SHA-256:

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `flashnext-arch-overlay.patch` | `bf9b00b89cf132c6db95bd51f7f3398b5362986c7c116e083631ac9cec8972b1` |
| `sycl-fused-mmvq-and-gpu-group.patch` | `4fb812ee13d0df5217b2a93f3d11e9cb98afccaf55d08963d16674da4ad2c836` |

The second patch is fused IQ3_S / IQ4_NL `MUL_MAT_ID` MMVQ plus on-device
expert-ID grouping. Grouping is on by default; `GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_MMID_GPU_GROUP=1`
turns it off. The n=5 prefill median 594.49 was taken before grouping; a matched
n=3 A/B later measured 599.48 vs 594.67 (+0.81%). Decode is unchanged.

Older split files `sycl-fused-mmvq-iq3s-iq4nl.patch` and
`sycl-mmid-gpu-group-20260901.patch` conflict if both are applied. Use the
combined kernel patch.

### 4. oneAPI

```bash
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh --force
```

### 5. Build the binary you will serve

FP32 binary (n=5 decode leader at 8K; also used for the 16K/128K FP32 map):

```bash
cmake -S . -B build-sycl \
  -DGGML_SYCL=ON \
  -DGGML_SYCL_F16=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx
cmake --build build-sycl --target llama-server -j
```

F16 binary (n=5 prefill leader at 16K; also used for the 8K/128K F16 map):

```bash
cmake -S . -B build-sycl-f16 \
  -DGGML_SYCL=ON \
  -DGGML_SYCL_F16=ON \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx
cmake --build build-sycl-f16 --target llama-server -j
```

Measured llama-server SHA-256 (pre-grouping fused MMVQ builds):

- FP32: `f56a838b0e1a16aa8a1321ce2a217c8f3e972e961cf0aca706f76f4d6421c98b`
- F16: `2da6e9fc89d9cb68368feb1a2e7ef1045ff705acb16721755ac1f72149dd1ee3`

### 6. Runtime env

```bash
export SYCL_PI_LEVEL_ZERO_USE_IMMEDIATE_COMMANDLISTS=0
export SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=0
export SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER=level_zero
export ZE_FLAT_DEVICE_HIERARCHY=COMPOSITE
```

Set each card's power cap through the `xe` hwmon `power1_cap`. Confirm with
`sycl-ls` that SYCL0 / SYCL1 are the two B70s.

### 7. Serve

Shared flags for every context size:

```text
-m "$MODEL"
--device SYCL0,SYCL1 --tensor-split 1,1 --split-mode layer -ngl 99
-ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU' -fa on -t 6 -tb 14 -np 1
--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q4_1
--no-warmup --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

**Sampling — Hugging Face card defaults** (`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`). Serve with
the card's values as server-side defaults so clients that omit parameters get
recommended behavior:

| Mode | `--temp` | `--top-p` | `--top-k` | `--min-p` | `--presence-penalty` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Thinking (default; this page's MTP recipe) | 1.0 | 0.95 | 20 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| Non-thinking (`chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`) | 0.7 | 0.80 | 20 | 0.0 | 1.5 |

Thinking-mode line to append to any serve command below:

```text
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
```

For non-thinking serving use `--temp 0.7 --top-p 0.80 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--presence-penalty 1.5` instead (card: presence_penalty may be raised 0–2 against
endless repetition; higher values can cause language mixing).

`-ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU'` pins the N-gram table (shard `00002`, Q5_1)
to host memory — see "N-gram (per-layer token embedding) table" above. It is
never loaded into VRAM.

Prompt caching is on (llama.cpp default). The published n=5 cells were measured with `--no-cache-prompt` added (cache off is for cold-input benchmarks only; serve with cache on).

Only `-c` and `-b` / `--ubatch-size` change:

| Context | `-c` | `-b` / `--ubatch-size` | Binary for the published n=5 cell |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 8K | 8192 | 512 | FP32 (`build-sycl`) |
| 16K | 16384 | 3072 | F16 (`build-sycl-f16`) |
| 128K | 131072 | 1024 | either; n=5 leaders were not 128K |

`-b 1536+` at 128K was rejected (`n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99`).
Do not pass `--no-mmap` or `--mlock` on this GGUF. `-fa on` is required:
`q4_1` V refuses flash-attention off.

8K (FP32 binary) — n=5 decode **23.38**:

```bash
./build-sycl/bin/llama-server -m "$MODEL" \
  --device SYCL0,SYCL1 --tensor-split 1,1 --split-mode layer -ngl 99 \
  -ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU' -c 8192 -fa on -t 6 -tb 14 -np 1 \
  -b 512 --ubatch-size 512 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q4_1 \
  --no-warmup --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

16K (F16 binary) — n=5 prefill **594.49**:

```bash
./build-sycl-f16/bin/llama-server -m "$MODEL" \
  --device SYCL0,SYCL1 --tensor-split 1,1 --split-mode layer -ngl 99 \
  -ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU' -c 16384 -fa on -t 6 -tb 14 -np 1 \
  -b 3072 --ubatch-size 3072 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q4_1 \
  --no-warmup --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

128K (same F16 binary, smaller ubatch):

```bash
./build-sycl-f16/bin/llama-server -m "$MODEL" \
  --device SYCL0,SYCL1 --tensor-split 1,1 --split-mode layer -ngl 99 \
  -ot 'per_layer_token_embd=CPU' -c 131072 -fa on -t 6 -tb 14 -np 1 \
  -b 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q4_1 \
  --no-warmup --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

### 8. Smoke

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"flash-next","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly B70-FLASH-OK"}],"max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}'
```

## Context map (n=3)

Same C1 contract. 8K cannot hold a 9096-token prompt. Decode at p512 stays
~23 tok/s through 128K.

| Build | Context | Batch | p512 decode | p512 cold input | p9096 decode | p9096 cold input |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP32 | 8K | 512 | 23.38 | 183.17 | — | — |
| FP32 | 16K | 3072 | 23.37 | 183.61 | 20.25 | 478.71 |
| FP32 | 128K | 1024 | 23.54 | 183.38 | 20.41 | 353.95 |
| F16 | 8K | 512 | 22.96 | 191.55 | — | — |
| F16 | 16K | 3072 | 23.31 | 192.64 | 20.40 | 593.98 |
| F16 | 128K | 1024 | 23.06 | 195.57 | 20.25 | 398.02 |

JSON: [`n3-context-map.json`](../../results/qwen38-flash-next-dual-b70-c1/n3-context-map.json).

## LocalMaxxing

`APPROVED` means accepted self-report, not independent reproduction. Platform
`quantization` is `IQ3_S`; mixed IQ3_S/IQ4_NL is in the notes.

| Cell | `tokSOut` | `tokSPrefill` | Context | Run |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| FP32 p512/g128 | 23.38 | 183.98 | 8192 | `cmtigo30804dyp401alu7nger` |
| F16 p9096/g128 | 20.34 | 594.49 | 16384 | `cmtigo39n04e2p401eumx5joo` |
| MTP+kernel p512/g128 code (matched) | 33.25 | — | 8192 | `cmtwyygmq0ah0ps01vvutjf7u` |
| MTP warm p512/g128 | 27.71 | 173.2 | 8192 | `cmtwkbb6j0af5ps01d3eta1lj` |
| F16 p9096/g128 (new build) | 22.96 | 585.9 | 16384 | `cmtwkbbgr0af9ps01dhv7ntgu` |

Receipts: [`localmaxxing-receipts.json`](../../results/qwen38-flash-next-dual-b70-c1/localmaxxing-receipts.json).

## Sparse attention for the QSA layers (screen, 2026-09-26)

Upstream llama.cpp [#28796](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28796) (merged
2026-09-25) adds an opt-in sparse path for single-token decode: instead of scanning the
whole KV of the full-attention layers, it gathers only the rows the QSA top-k mask
leaves finite (~2,051 of 28,928 at 28K occupied context on this model).

- Enable: `GGML_SYCL_SPARSE_FA=1` (plus `GGML_SYCL_SPARSE_FA_DEBUG=1` to log gather
  counts). Default off upstream.
- **Prerequisite the pinned build lacks:** the feature reads the FA node's `n_kv_max`
  op-parameter, which only graph builders after the `ggml_flash_attn_ext_set_n_kv_max`
  plumbing set it. Our pinned `9723942` tree leaves it at 0, so the path never engages
  there. Verify engagement by the `[FA-SPARSE]` debug lines before believing any number.
- Measured on this recipe's placement (32K ctx, heavier CPU expert offload, C-S-C
  counterbalanced, n=3/arm, lab screen — see
[WHAT-WORKED](../WHAT-WORKED.md)): **+7–9 % decode at occupied 28K**, prefill
  unchanged, correctness trio clean, no mask overflow. The gain is bounded by this
  placement's CPU-resident experts; a lighter placement or deeper context should show
  more. Upstream's author measured +52 % at 28.6K on a full-GPU single-card placement.

Not yet part of the pinned recipe: rebasing the pinned tree past the `n_kv_max`
plumbing and a deeper-cell confirmation are the remaining steps.

## Limits

- Layer split across two cards, not vLLM tensor parallel.
- vLLM-XPU, AutoRound, and the official BF16 checkpoint are not this recipe.
- Speed here is not a quality or logit-parity result.

Catalog: [`docs/BENCHMARK-CATALOG.md`](../BENCHMARK-CATALOG.md).
Pins: [`identities.json`](../../results/qwen38-flash-next-dual-b70-c1/identities.json).

docs.title: Flash-Next: IQ3_S versus IQ3_XXS on two B70s
docs.text:
# Flash-Next: IQ3_S versus IQ3_XXS on two B70s

[Family index](README.md) · [Dual-B70 topology](../DUAL-B70-TP2.md) · [Raw evidence](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/summary.json)

## 1. Result

IQ3_S runs on two Arc Pro B70s with XeStrata `xe0.1.45-1`, a 262,144-token configured context, int8 attention cache and pipelined MTP4. In matched C1, thinking-off tests, its median code decode was **86.7 tok/s**, versus **86.8 tok/s** for IQ3_XXS: 34 prompt tokens, 512 output tokens, three measured runs after one warm-up. At 32,429 prompt tokens, median prefill was **1,879.5 versus 1,894.2 tok/s**. IQ3_S is the largest quant in the pinned ISTA repository listing, and fits this setup, but GPU 1 is nearly full. Both quants passed 5/6 small answer checks without thinking and 6/6 with high effort. These checks establish no general quality advantage for IQ3_S.

## 2. What you need

| Item | Measured setup / requirement |
|---|---|
| GPUs | Two Intel Arc Pro B70s, nominal 32 GB each; first stage layers 0–23, second stage layers 24–47 |
| Power | As-found caps: GPU 0 **180 W**, GPU 1 **230 W**. The launcher did not change them. This is not a matched-180-W-per-card test. |
| Host RAM | 64 GB class host; engine memory guard reported 60.7 GiB total. CPU expert kernels used AVX2. |
| Disk | IQ3_S first shard: 54,817,524,224 bytes (51.05 GiB). Shared lookup shard: 28,800,138,432 bytes (26.82 GiB). Native pack about 1.43 GiB, MTP files about 787 MiB, CPU vision projector about 866 MiB. Allow roughly 81 GiB for a fresh serving set. |
| Model source | [`ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09), revision `ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09` |
| Runtime | [XeStrata](https://github.com/MistvVK/XeStrata), packaged SYCL engine reporting `xe0.1.45-1`; host oneAPI compiler and MKL 2026.1 library paths; no Docker image in this run |
| Launcher | B70 Launcher 0.6.19; separate `qwen38-flashnext-iq3s` recipe and temporary per-launch config |

Exact engine, server, expert-profile and model SHA256 values are in [`artifacts.json`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/artifacts.json). The measured binary is identified by its digest, not by an assumed upstream commit. Its engine SHA256 is `d633e321ba22179c9b1515840b922a49d0d426caea4819237fa2350f4c92e450`.

The existing IQ3_XXS lookup shard and the IQ3_S repository's second shard have the same SHA256, `316b46f3a2dbd68c900f43136ab9449f9dcc3725dfd8c794847c204bc161e113`. Reuse those bytes through an IQ3_S-named symlink. Do not copy or download another 26.82 GiB unnecessarily.

## 3. Timeline

Clock times below are local UTC+02:00 on 2026-10-19. Missing clock measurements are labeled rather than reconstructed from estimates.

| Time / elapsed | Step | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Before the timed native comparison; clocks not captured | Two research agents failed to start with `No model selected`; continued inline | No agent findings used |
| Before download; clock not captured | Found insufficient free space; removed the stale Signal AP-Q4_K_XL download with operator approval | Preserved the running IQ3_XXS artifacts |
| Download elapsed **32m20.62s**; start/end clock not captured | Downloaded the pinned 51.05 GiB IQ3_S first shard over Wi-Fi | Completed; SHA256 matched the repository LFS digest |
| 09:30:27 | Submitted nine previously catalog-blocked results | IDs 265–273, read back through the API |
| 09:33:14 | Opened [IntelInside catalog PR #116](https://github.com/labscommunity/intelinside/pull/116) | Correct IQ3 boards and Strata runtime requested |
| 09:34:40 | Submitted two historical llama.cpp Flash-Next results with separate workload coordinates | IDs 274–275, read back through the API |
| Catalog validation, clock not captured | First validator run could not import `vite` | Reused the installed dependency directory; catalog validation then passed |
| 09:39:00 | Started native-context IQ3_XXS through the new launch wrapper | Source config remained separate from launch overrides |
| Before 09:40:50 | Started benchmark before the HTTP endpoint was ready | `ConnectionRefusedError`; waited for readiness before retrying |
| 09:40:50–09:42:43 | IQ3_XXS native speed suite, including warm-ups | Twelve saved responses |
| After native speed suite | IQ3_XXS answer checks, none and high effort | 5/6 and 6/6 |
| 10:03:37; failed launch elapsed **9.91s** | First IQ3_S launch pointed `--ple-gguf` at the old alias | `native dense: duplicate split shard number` |
| **10:04:49; successful launch elapsed 2m37s** | **Used the IQ3_S-named second-shard symlink for `--ple-gguf`** | **Ready; launcher smoke answered in 0.718s** |
| 10:07:44–10:09:40 | IQ3_S native measured speed rows | Three measured rows per case after warm-up |
| After native speed suite | IQ3_S answer checks, none and high effort; generic `loaded` alias | 5/6, 6/6, and `4` for 2+2 |
| During allocation/client checks; clocks not captured | `ps -C` was unsupported; a remote config write was refused because the read was truncated; unauthenticated UI GET returned 403 | Used the known PID, reconstructed the complete config before writing, and used the documented nonce bootstrap |
| During XeCores publication; clock not captured | Same-commit cookbook sync reported missing pin constants even though both existed | Fixed presence validation; same-pin sync, pin gate, build and nine-page navigation gate passed |

Native baseline engine-start to final measured IQ3_S speed row: **30m40.51s**. This interval overlaps the weight download and other work; it is not pure benchmark compute time. Exactly timed failed IQ3_S load: **9.91s**. The premature benchmark and dependency failure were not separately clocked, so total time lost to failures and full-session wall time are **not measured**.

## 4. Step by step

### 1. Download and verify the first shard

Set paths for your checkout and storage. The examples reuse a working IQ3_XXS installation and its MTP, expert profile and CPU vision files.

```bash
export XE=/path/to/XeStrata
export MODEL_DIR=/your/disk/qwen38-flashnext-iq3s/IQ3_S
export PACK=/your/disk/strata-packs/iq3s
export OLD_LOOKUP=/your/disk/IQ3_XXS/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00002-of-00002.gguf
export FIRST="$MODEL_DIR/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf"
export SECOND="$MODEL_DIR/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00002-of-00002.gguf"
mkdir -p "$MODEL_DIR"
curl --fail --location --retry 3 --continue-at - --output "$FIRST" \
  https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/resolve/ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09/IQ3_S/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf
printf '%s  %s\n' 4c1eb2ceb4915e1192f4f386021897bde56a97f40a0bb78bb86465e0f7d2aca3 "$FIRST" | sha256sum -c -
printf '%s  %s\n' 316b46f3a2dbd68c900f43136ab9449f9dcc3725dfd8c794847c204bc161e113 "$OLD_LOOKUP" | sha256sum -c -
ln -s "$OLD_LOOKUP" "$SECOND"
```

On this workstation, adding `--interface wlx7419f81751a9` selected the operator-requested Wi-Fi connection. Use your own interface name if needed. The symlink command assumes the new link does not already exist.

### 2. Build a separate native pack

```bash
"$XE/.venv/bin/python" "$XE/tools/iq_pack.py" --gguf "$FIRST" --out "$PACK"
```

Observed output: 1,079 tensors, 302 served natively, zero tensors in `extra.bin`, 1.43 GiB arena. The tokenizer builder wrote vocabulary and chat-template files. Do not reuse the IQ3_XXS pack or generate a second full `experts.bin` for this mmap route.

### 3. Derive the IQ3_S config without changing IQ3_XXS

```bash
export BASE_CONFIG="$HOME/.config/xestrata/xestrata-iq3_xxs.json"
export NEW_CONFIG="$HOME/.config/xestrata/xestrata-iq3_s.json"
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
from pathlib import Path
cfg = json.loads(Path(os.environ['BASE_CONFIG']).read_text())
args = cfg['args']
for flag, value in [('--native', os.environ['FIRST']), ('--ple-gguf', os.environ['SECOND']),
                    ('--pack', os.environ['PACK']), ('--max-context', '262144')]:
    args[args.index(flag) + 1] = value
for flag in ('--rope-scaling', '--rope-scale', '--yarn-orig-ctx'):
    if flag in args:
        i = args.index(flag)
        del args[i:i + 2]
cfg['tokenizer'] = os.environ['PACK'] + '/tokenizer'
cfg['model_name'] = 'qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s'
cfg['log'] = str(Path.home() / '.local/state/xestrata/xestrata-iq3_s.log')
if cfg.get('vision'):
    cfg['vision']['model'] = os.environ['FIRST']
Path(os.environ['NEW_CONFIG']).write_text(json.dumps(cfg, indent=2) + '\n')
PY
```

Keep `--layer-split 24`, `--pipeline-windows 2`, `--spec 4`, `--kv int8`, the MTP directory and expert profile matched across arms. The explicit lookup path must be the same spelling as the shard discovered beside `--native`; the older path alias causes the duplicate-shard failure even when its bytes are identical.

### 4. Select and launch the recipe

The shipped recipe contains the measured workstation's local paths. For another disk layout, set `model_path`, `config_file`, `py_exe`, `server_script`, `vision_exe` and `mmproj` in local `recipe_overrides` before launching; see the launcher's recipe-format documentation.

```bash
b70 launch qwen38-flashnext-iq3s -e xestrata --ctx 262144 --vision --effort none
# Text-only launch:
# b70 launch qwen38-flashnext-iq3s -e xestrata --ctx 262144 --no-vision
```

Wait for `serving` before measuring. `--effort` sets the launch default through the temporary config. API requests can select `reasoning_effort: none|low|medium|high|xhigh` without reloading weights. `--vision` enables the CPU encoder; accepting an image request does not establish image-answer accuracy.

### 5. Run both arms with the same protocol

From the cookbook root, with IQ3_S serving:

```bash
python3 benchmarks/qwen38-strata-quant-compare.py --label iq3_s-native262k-vision-cpu --output results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/iq3_s-native
python3 benchmarks/qwen38-strata-quant-compare.py --suite quality --repeats 1 --label iq3_s-native262k-vision-cpu --output results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/iq3_s-native-quality
python3 benchmarks/qwen38-strata-quant-compare.py --suite quality --effort high --repeats 1 --label iq3_s-native262k-high --output results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/iq3_s-native-quality-high
```

Stop this recipe, launch `qwen38-flashnext -e xestrata --ctx 262144 --vision --effort none`, and repeat with `iq3_xxs` labels and output folders. Use fresh folders for a new campaign rather than overwriting the committed evidence.

## 5. Every fix

| # | Literal symptom / observed problem | Cause | Fix | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `No model selected` from research agents | Agent configuration unavailable | Continued the research inline | Source paths, catalog responses and saved run evidence used directly |
| 2 | Insufficient space for a 51.05 GiB new shard | Storage occupied by a stale Signal download | Removed that download with operator approval; reused the lookup shard | Full pinned download completed and SHA256 matched |
| 3 | `Cannot find package 'vite'` | New catalog worktree lacked dependencies | Linked the existing installed `node_modules` | Catalog validator passed: 52 hardware, 51 models, 26 quants, 9 runtimes |
| 4 | `ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused` | Benchmark began while weights were loading | Waited for the HTTP models endpoint | Twelve native IQ3_XXS speed responses saved |
| 5 | `native dense: duplicate split shard number` | Explicit PLE path used an old alias, so the same split shard was appended twice | Pointed PLE at the IQ3_S-named symlink beside shard 1 | IQ3_S loaded and completed all 36 comparison requests |
| 6 | Earlier dry-build implementation changed vision in the source config; effort was passed as an unsupported server flag | Launch controls modified shared state / targeted the wrong interface | Temporary per-launch config; effort, context and vision applied there | 348 launcher tests passed, including source-config preservation; native launches and generic-alias request succeeded |
| 7 | Result 240 classified IQ3_XXS as `q2_0` under llama.cpp | Missing catalog quant/runtime entries had been replaced with incorrect labels | Withdrew result 240; requested proper entries in PR #116 | DELETE returned 200; new submission command refuses to post until catalog sync |
| 8 | `official-results.js pin constants not found — G-PIN would fail` | Vendor script treated an unchanged replacement as a missing constant | Validate both constant patterns before replacement, not whether the text changes | Same-commit `sync:cookbook` passed; 30 docs and 50 benchmark records vendored; G-PIN and G-NAV passed |
| 9 | `Refusing to overwrite ... with an incomplete read projection` | Remote config exceeded the read output cap | Read the omitted tail, reconstructed all 52,696 bytes, then changed three context values | Remote YAML parsed; loaded-model context asserted at 262,144; remote models endpoint returned IQ3_S |
| 10 | `ps: unsupported option '-C'` | The available command wrapper does not support process-name selection | Queried the known engine PID and its `smaps_rollup` | Main-engine resident/file-backed/anonymous/swap figures recorded |
| 11 | `unauthorized request` on the launcher root URL | Browser had no launcher authentication cookie | Used authenticated `POST /api/window` and its one-use nonce URL | Chromium displayed the new on-disk IQ3_S recipe and its context controls |

## 6. Verification

Each native quant arm has **36 saved responses**: 12 speed responses (three cases, one warm-up plus three measured runs), 12 thinking-off answer checks, and 12 high-effort answer checks. Answer scores use six measured checks per mode, excluding each warm-up. All measured speed responses report zero prompt-cache hits.

| Evidence | Location |
|---|---|
| Raw requests, full responses, token counts and engine timings | [`iq3_xxs-native/`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/iq3_xxs-native/) and [`iq3_s-native/`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/iq3_s-native/) |
| Answer checks | Corresponding `*-native-quality/` and `*-native-quality-high/` folders in the same evidence directory |
| Compiled values and allocation snapshots | [`summary.json`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/summary.json), [`allocation.json`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/allocation.json) |
| Generic loaded-model request | [`loaded-smoke.json`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/loaded-smoke.json): model resolved to IQ3_S and answered `4` |
| Historical upload receipts | [`intelinside-receipts.json`](../../results/qwen38-strata-quant-20261019/intelinside-receipts.json): 11 new results, each read back |

The launcher UI was exercised in Chromium: IQ3_S appeared as a selectable on-disk model with its XeStrata route, 262,144-token default and 350,000-token experimental ceiling. No UI unit tests were added. Launcher release verification checked 76 packaged files.

Publication checks also passed the four existing benchmark-catalog tests and the renderer's 50-record current-output check. XeCores preview rendered the quant guide and linked the 0.6.19 tarball, checksum and manifest. The cookbook document allowlist now includes the Flash-Next family index, this guide and the llama.cpp guide. [Launcher release 0.6.19](https://github.com/SergiioB/b70-launcher/releases/tag/v0.6.19) has SHA256 `fb46ef1e553b9c7a62a2643f562ce54ea246be3c17e04aa8b20f545d859e6594`.

## 7. Results and claim boundary

### Matched native-context speed

C1, temperature 0, `reasoning_effort: none`, MTP4, K=24, two pipeline windows, int8 attention cache, 262,144-token configured capacity. Medians of three measured rows after warm-up. Rates use the engine's `timings`, not client time-to-first-token or wall-clock throughput. Power caps were 180/230 W as found; this was a sequential A-then-B comparison, not an interleaved or iso-power study.

| Workload / metric | IQ3_XXS | IQ3_S |
|---|---:|---:|
| Code decode, P34/G512 | 86.8 tok/s | 86.7 tok/s |
| Train explanation decode, P59/G512, thinking disabled | 93.3 tok/s | 93.2 tok/s |
| Prefill, P32,429, output cap 128 | 1,894.2 tok/s | 1,879.5 tok/s |
| Small answer checks, thinking off | 5/6 | 5/6 |
| Small answer checks, high effort | 6/6 | 6/6 |

The long-prefill outputs ended naturally: IQ3_XXS produced 13–17 tokens and IQ3_S 36–54 tokens. Their decode speeds are therefore not a matched generated-token-length comparison and are not used as headline decode results. The code outputs reached their 512-token cap; this measures generation speed, not a completed or executed LRU-cache implementation.

Both thinking-off arms answered `50` instead of `48` on the exact-answer average-speed question. Both high-effort arms answered correctly. Changing quant did not fix that failure in this small set.

### Disk, RAM and VRAM

| Allocation | IQ3_XXS | IQ3_S |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU 0 dashboard usage | 23.1 GiB | 27.7 GiB |
| GPU 1 dashboard usage | 29.2 GiB | 31.7 GiB |
| Expert cache, GPU 0 / GPU 1 | 17.72 / 22.24 GiB | 22.14 / 24.51 GiB |
| Resident expert slots | 24,576 / 24,576 | 24,488 / 24,576 |
| Main engine resident RAM snapshot | 39.7 GiB | 43.1 GiB |
| Main engine swap snapshot | 439 MiB | 0 MiB |
| First shard | 43.81 GiB | 51.05 GiB |

These are snapshots, not peak-memory measurements. Whole-card usage includes buffers and other allocations. Most engine RAM is clean, file-backed mapped weight data, not private heap; Linux can reclaim it. Disk, RAM and VRAM contain overlapping copies and must not be added as unique model size. The shared lookup stays on disk and is read through the PLE path. A separate CPU vision encoder is not included in the main-engine RAM snapshot.

IQ3_S fits, with 88 expert slots outside its resident cache and little GPU 1 headroom. IQ3_XXS remains a reasonable choice when extra memory margin matters. The measured speed difference is below 1%; this run does not establish a useful speed advantage for either quant.

### IntelInside publication

| Results | Status |
|---|---|
| Bolt SYCL / IQ2_XXS | [265](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/265), [266](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/266), [267](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/267) published |
| Bolt AutoRound TP2 | [268](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/268)–[271](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/271) published |
| Qwen3.8-27B FP8 / EXL3 | [272](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/272), [273](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/273) published; FP8 notes identify the synthetic diagnostic workload |
| Historical Flash-Next llama.cpp | [274](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/274), [275](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/275) published under custom runtime 16; prompt/decode coordinates kept separate |
| New Strata IQ3 results | [276](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/276) (IQ3_XXS, 86.8 tok/s) and [277](https://www.intelinside.ai/results/277) (IQ3_S, 86.7 tok/s) published under custom runtime 17 (`XeStrata xe0.1.45-1 SYCL + MTP4`) |

Following maintainer merge of [catalog PR #116](https://github.com/labscommunity/intelinside/pull/116) and database sync, `benchmarks/submit-qwen38-strata-quants.py --submit` registered XeStrata under the new `strata` runtime and submitted the two matched C1 measurements. Both results use the new dedicated `iq3_xxs` and `iq3_s` boards with paired P34/G512 prompt and decode rates from the same runs.

**Not tested:**

- Long-context retrieval or perplexity at the configured 262K capacity; the longest measured prompt here was 32,429 tokens.
- IQ3_S at 350K YaRN, its long-context accuracy, or a claim that extrapolation degradation is negligible.
- Broad coding-task accuracy, KL divergence, BF16 parity, sustained thermal behavior or concurrent requests.
- Correct visual understanding. Earlier small color-image replies were wrong; image-input metadata and HTTP success are not correctness proof.
- Equal power caps, energy per token, a quant-by-quant autotuning search, or a larger quant from another repository.

This is self-reported workstation evidence with saved requests and timings. It supports the stated serving configuration and workloads, not a model-wide quality ranking. Earlier external 122.2 tok/s claims are not reproduced by this campaign and are not used as local measurements. The retained `iq3_xxs/` folder is an earlier 350K configuration run and is not the native-context comparison arm.

## 8. If you do this again

Reuse the verified lookup shard and MTP files, download only the new first shard, make a separate native pack, use the matching new lookup filename, and wait for `serving`. On this Wi-Fi download, weights took 32m20s; hashing took 1m46s, packing 5.23s, successful IQ3_S launch 2m37s, and its speed-plus-answer campaign 2m30s. Allow about 40 minutes on the same connection; disk/cache state and network speed can change that substantially.

## 9. Adapting it

For another quant, regenerate its pack and change both the native shard and tokenizer. Share the lookup only after comparing its complete digest; matching filenames or sizes are insufficient. Preserve prompt text, token caps, effort, cache behavior, GPU selection and power settings before comparing rates. Keep native context as the measured default; treat YaRN capacity and vision accuracy as separate experiments. Publish under the actual quant and runtime, and retain failed attempts with their literal errors.

**Keeper decision (2026-10-19):** the workstation now keeps **IQ3_XXS as its
only Flash-Next quant**; the IQ3_S first shard and pack were deleted (about
53 GiB freed). Equal speed, equal check scores, more disk, more VRAM and a
nearly full second GPU bought nothing measurable. Section 8 restores IQ3_S in
about 40 minutes if a denser quant is ever wanted again.

docs.title: Ripple-65B Preview on two Arc Pro B70 cards (llama.cpp SYCL)
docs.text:
# Ripple-65B Preview on two Arc Pro B70 cards (llama.cpp SYCL)

Ricursive's [Ripple-65B Preview](https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview)
(65B dense, Apache-2.0, released 2026-11-04) runs on two B70 cards with stock llama.cpp.
Use `-sm tensor` and **build llama.cpp with `GGML_SYCL_F16=ON`**: the flag nearly
triples prompt processing (720 vs 218 tok/s on `Q4_K_M`) and leaves decode unchanged.
Measured 2026-11-08, status **screen** (two repeats per cell, one where noted). Evidence:
[`results/ripple-65b/dual-b70-20261108/`](../../results/ripple-65b/dual-b70-20261108/)
(F16 off) and
[`results/ripple-65b/prefill-f16-20261108/`](../../results/ripple-65b/prefill-f16-20261108/) (F16 A/B).

| File · split · build | KV | Decode tok/s at 0 / 16K / 32K | Prefill tok/s (pp2048) at 0 / 16K / 32K |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`Q4_K_M` · `-sm tensor` · F16 ON** | f16 | **14.5 / 13.2 / 12.5** | **720 / 601 / 527** |
| `Q4_K_M` · `-sm tensor` · F16 OFF | f16 | 14.6 / 13.2 / 12.5 | 218 / 208 / 200 |
| `AD-IQ4_XS` · `-sm tensor` · F16 ON | f16 | 12.5 / 11.2 / 10.0 | 643 / 549 / 443 |
| `AD-IQ4_XS` · `-sm tensor` · F16 OFF | f16 | 13.2 / — / — | 214 / — / — |
| `AD-IQ4_XS` · `-sm layer` · F16 ON | q8_0 | 10.3 / — / — | 496 / — / — |

- The F16 build flag changes prefill only: `Q4_K_M` decode is 14.5–14.6 tok/s either way.
  On `AD-IQ4_XS` the F16 build costs ~0.7 tok/s of decode for the prefill win.
  Same commit (`b12195-3-gf477f795c`), rebuilt with `-DGGML_SYCL_F16=ON`.
  Use `-b 2048 -ub 2048`; at `-ub 512` the F16 build manages 643 tok/s pp on `AD-IQ4_XS`.
- Earlier numbers on this page (13.3 / 189 tok/s, F16 off, `pp512`) are superseded.

Quality smoke on the `-sm tensor` server: exact-answer battery 9/9 (6 canaries + 3 prompts
at ~8K tokens), and a `merge_intervals` coding prompt answered with code whose asserts pass
when executed. That is a smoke test, not a quality ranking.

## Serve it

```bash
# llama.cpp b12167 or newer (Ripple support, PR #31692); we used b12195-3-gf477f795c.
# Build with: cmake -S . -B build-sycl -DGGML_SYCL=ON -DGGML_SYCL_F16=ON \
#   -DGGML_SYCL_GRAPH=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx \
#   -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF
curl -L -o Ripple-65B-Preview-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  https://huggingface.co/ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview-GGUF/resolve/main/Ripple-65B-Preview-Q4_K_M.gguf
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh --force
ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR='level_zero:0,1' ZE_FLAT_DEVICE_HIERARCHY=COMPOSITE \
llama-server -m Ripple-65B-Preview-Q4_K_M.gguf -ngl 99 -fa on -sm tensor \
  -b 2048 -ub 2048 -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -c 32768 -t 8 --jinja --port 8050

- `Q4_K_M` (38.8 GB) is the speed pick on two cards. `AD-IQ4_XS` (38.7 GB, 4.78 bpw) is
  AtomicChat's imatrix file; their card reports 2.5× lower KL than the plain `Q4_K_M` at
  the same size. Either needs both cards.
- Open question for long sessions (2026-11-10): a later private run switched to `-sm layer`
  after seeing host memory (RSS) of `llama-server` grow with every generated token under
  `-sm tensor` on this build. That observation was not retained, so it is neither proven nor
  ruled out. If you run long sessions, watch `ps -o rss= -p <pid>` of the server; `-sm layer`
  avoids the question at about 29 % less decode speed.
- Keep f16 KV with `-sm tensor`: llama.cpp issue
  [#26409](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/26409) reports hangs with quantized
  KV in tensor mode. We did not test quantized KV with `-sm tensor`.
- Four of every five layers use 1,024-token sliding-window attention, so decode loses only
  12 % from empty context to 32K.
- `--jinja` uses the chat template embedded in the GGUF (reasoning and tools).

## Deep context: 256K serves, and the session does not sag

Measured 2026-11-09 with the real-content depth harness (`depth_bench.py`, code + prose
corpora, 512-token answers, greedy, 2 reps per cell; spread across reps < 0.5 tok/s).
Evidence and the session log:
[`results/ripple-65b/depth-256k-session-20261109/`](../../results/ripple-65b/depth-256k-session-20261109/).

![Decode by context depth, Ripple vs Qwen3.8-27B](../assets/ripple-qwen-depth-256k-20261109.png)

| Prompt depth | 0 | 32K | 128K | 256K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Decode tok/s | 14.5 | 12.7 | 9.5 | 7.2 |
| Prefill tok/s (tokens/TTFT, real content) | — | 187 | 228 | 162 |
| 256K context fits? | | | | yes — `-c 262144`, f16 KV, 39.4 GB weights split over both cards |

- Ripple answers streamed as `reasoning_content` on these cells (its template ignores
  `enable_thinking`); rates cover all streamed tokens.
- **Session stability** (the number a long coding session actually feels):
  one conversation, 128K-token seed document, then 10 follow-up turns. Decode was
  **9.65–9.71 tok/s on every turn** — 0 % drift end to end — and turn TTFT was ~9 s
  because the KV prefix cache absorbs the history. Per-64-token windows inside each turn
  are flat too. No cliff, no ramp-down.
- Prefill caveat: a cold 256K prompt takes ~24 min at ~162 tok/s. Long-context use wants
  a warm prefix (server prompt cache), not repeated cold 256K prompts.


## Claim boundary

- Two B70 cards on PCIe 4.0 x8/x8 (CPU lanes), caps 180 W and 230 W as found, single
  stream, `llama-bench -ngl 99 -fa 1 -t 8 -b 2048 -ub 2048 -p 2048 -n 128 -r 2` per cell
  (F16-ON cells: one repeat at depth, two at 0). Depth cells above 32K use the separate
  real-content harness described in the deep-context section. A background CPU-only
  service was active during the depth session; GPU work was exclusive.
- Two files (`Q4_K_M`, `AD-IQ4_XS`). Ricursive publishes no sampling defaults for the
  Preview; the smoke used temperature 0.
- Card draw during the `-sm tensor` sweep averaged ~367 W for both cards together.
